name: @tocharianou/aws-network-mcp

tools.name: list_vpcs
tools.description: List all VPCs in an AWS region. Shows VPC ID, CIDR block, state, default flag, and tags. Ideal for: discovering VPC infrastructure before detailed analysis, finding VPC IDs needed for other tools, auditing VPC inventory.

region.description: AWS region to list VPCs from (e.g. us-east-1). Defaults to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_vpc_network_details
tools.description: Get comprehensive VPC network configuration: subnets, route tables, internet gateway, NAT gateways, network ACLs, and VPC endpoints. Ideal for: analyzing network topology, investigating connectivity issues, checking internet exposure (IGW attached?), identifying missing routes or NACL blocks, confirming VPC endpoint configurations for AWS services.

vpcId.description: VPC ID to inspect. Example: "vpc-0123456789abcdef0". Use list_vpcs to discover VPC IDs.

region.description: AWS region where the VPC is located. Defaults to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_vpc_flow_logs
tools.description: Query VPC Flow Logs stored in CloudWatch Logs using Logs Insights. Supports filtering by action (ACCEPT/REJECT), source/destination IP, ports, and ENI. Ideal for: investigating blocked connections (filter action=REJECT), tracing traffic from a suspicious IP (srcaddr filter), analyzing lateral movement patterns, verifying security group effectiveness. REQUIRES: VPC Flow Logs must be enabled and sent to a CloudWatch Logs group.

vpcId.description: VPC ID to retrieve flow logs for. Example: "vpc-0123456789abcdef0".

timePeriod.description: How many minutes back to query (1–1440, default: 60). Note: flow logs have 5–15 min delay.

startTime.description: End time of the query window (ISO 8601, e.g. "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z"). Query window = startTime - timePeriod → startTime. Defaults to now.

entryLimit.description: Max flow log entries to return (1–1000, default: 100). Keep low to avoid token overflow.

action.description: Filter by traffic action. REJECT shows blocked connections.

srcaddr.description: Filter by source IP address (IPv4 or IPv6).

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: find_ip_address
tools.description: Locate an AWS Elastic Network Interface (ENI) by IP address (private or public). Returns ENI ID, VPC, subnet, availability zone, security groups, and attached resource. Ideal for: identifying which AWS resource owns a suspicious IP seen in CloudTrail or flow logs, correlating an attack source IP with an EC2 instance or Lambda function, starting network path analysis from a known IP.

ipAddress.description: IP address to locate (IPv4 or IPv6, private or public). Example: "10.0.1.45" or "54.239.28.85"

region.description: AWS region to search. Defaults to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION. Ignored when allRegions is true.

allRegions.description: If true, search all enabled AWS regions. Slower but comprehensive. Default: false.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).

tools.name: get_eni_details
tools.description: Get comprehensive ENI details: security group rules (inbound/outbound), network ACL rules, and route table entries for the associated subnet. Ideal for: analyzing why traffic is blocked (which security group rule denies it?), understanding the full network policy applied to an EC2 instance or Lambda, validating routing paths from a specific network interface.

eniId.description: Elastic Network Interface ID. Format: "eni-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx". Obtain from find_ip_address or VPC flow log entries (interface_id field).

region.description: AWS region where the ENI is located. Defaults to AWS_DEFAULT_REGION.

break_token_rule.description: Set to true to bypass token limits in critical situations (default: false).
